full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah, J: This first appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31.03.2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 59 of 1994 decreeing the suit.

2. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed the said title suit in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land on the averments, inter-alia, that the land of C.S. khatian No. 241 being plot No. 390/3940 measuring an area of 0568 ajutangsha originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya which was put to auction for arrear of rent in certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque, son of late Munshi Nowab Ali of 74, Mirpur, Dhaka on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and sale certificate was issued in favour of said Ali Ahmed on 19.11.1953. The auction purchaser (Ali Ahmed) got possession of the auction purchased land on 20.01.1954 through court. Ali Ahmed being in possession of the auction purchased land (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) for more than 12 years mutated his name in the Government record and paid rents accordingly; S.A. Khatian being No.197 and R.S. Khatian being No.1248 were prepared in his name. Ali Ahmed while had been in possession of the suit property died issueless on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, named, Khatibunnassa who inherited the entire suit property as her 4 annas share as his wife and the remaining 12 annas share because of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnesa being the 16 annas owner of the suit property died on 10.02.78 leaving behind her only full brother Abdul Mannan who inherited the entire property of his deceased sister. While Abdul Mannan had been in possession of the suit property as the 16 annas owner, by a registered heba-bil-ewaj dated 29.11.79 being No. 45060 transferred the suit property in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs being minors their father Abdul Majid as their natural guardian took over the possession of the transferred land. Thus the plaintiffs being the 16 annas owners of the suit property have been in peaceful possession thereof. Defendants having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by resorting to various tactics created forged papers and tried to take possession of the suit property forcibly, but due to the intervention of the respectable people of the mahalla failed. On 06.07.80 the defendants along with the process server of the Court and the police attacked (in the plaint in Bengali it has been written as “হামলা চালায়” in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs by showing a decree. The bailiff of the Court having seen the valid title documents of the plaintiffs failed to execute the decree in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. However, after making inquiry from the bailiff of the Court the father of the plaintiffs Abdul Mazid came to know that the defendants obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.79 in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. On further query the plaintiffs came to know that a so-called bainapatra to sell the suit property allegedly entered into by one Rasheda Begum, wife of Salimuddin of 321, Lalbag Road, Dhaka on 12.08.92 with the defendants was the basis of the said decree. Rasheda Begum went to Pakistan Via Nepal after liberation of Bangladesh, so the alleged bainapatra was fraudulent and was not legally enforceable in respect of the suit property. Rasheda Begum had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. Therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title to the suit property either on the basis of the bainapatra or their alleged purchase. The plaintiffs themselves and through their predecessor have been in possession of the suit property for more than 12 years since the purchase of the same in auction. The defendants got a kabala executed and registered in their names through court in execution of the ex-parte decree passed in the said suit, but by the said kabala they did not acquire right, tide and interest in the suit property. As neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979, the decree passed therein suit was not binding upon them. The defendants were not entitled to get any relief by way of execution of the decree through Title Execution No. 3 of 1980 without filing a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession on payment of a advalorem court fees. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction which was decreed on 28.03.84 on contest. Against the said decree the defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka who heard the appeal allowed the same by judgment and decree dated 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in the said appeal the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before this Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.05.92 and thus decree passed by the appellate court was up-held. Against the judgment and order passed in the said civil revision the plaintiffs filed Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1972 before the Appellate Division. The leave petition was dismissed by the Appellate Division observing as under:

"The learned Subordinate Judge in dismissing the suit, inter-alia, found that since complicated question of law as well as facts was involved in the suit a simple suit for permanent injunction was not maintainable and the plaintiffs ought to have instituted a suit (sic) establishment of their title. The learned Judge of the High Court Division upon independently examining the facts of the case similarly case (sic) to the finding that a disputed question of title was very much involved in the matter chich cannot be decided in a suit for permanent injunction. The suit was not maintainable."

3. When the defendants tried to take possession of the suit property through Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 without filing any suit for title and recovery of khash possession the plaintiffs on 27.10.93 filed an application under Order 21, rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the execution case. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 29.01.94 rejected the said application. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property through the said execution case, they were telling the people of the Mahalla that in an opportune moment they would take possession of the suit property by dispossessing the plaintiffs therefrom. The defendants are very powerful and rich persons having so many `goondas' at their disposal and they might dispossess the plaintiffs at any time causing irreparable loss and damage to them. The cause of action for the suit arose on 21.10.93 when the defendants along with the bailiff asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them and the same was continuing.

4. By amending the plaint 2 (two) prayers were added being prayers ka(1) and ka(2). The prayers are as under:

(a) for a declaration that the plaintiffs were not bound by the judgment and decree dated 15.11.79 passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 of the court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka.

(b) for permanent injunction restraining the defendants from evicting the plaintiffs from the suit property and thus dispossess them therefrom through Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 of the court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka.

5. The plaintiffs amended the plaint further praying for declaration of title, recovery of khash possession and for mesne profit from 16.09.97 to till the delivery of possession of the suit property to them along with interest at the rate of 16 % stating, inter-alia, that during the pendency of the suit the plaintiffs became major on 07.10.95 and 15.10.96 respectively. While the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing the defendants having understood that they would be defeated in the suit they along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.97 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom and looted away the household articles worth taka 6,00,000/00. In the similar way the defendants also looted away the goods from 10 (ten) family rooms and 13 (thirteen) shops in the suit property and took possession thereof. The plaintiffs used to get rent from the tenants of the said family rooms and shops to the tune of taka 26,000/00 per month. After the incident Mr. Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs lodged a complaint with Lalbagh Police Station informing the police the said fact of illegal eviction and looting of goods by the defendants and their terrorist which being treated as First Information Report was registered as Lalbag Police Station Case No. 32(9)97 under sections 144/447/44 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants one Wazir Ahmed also lodged a complaint with the said police station which was registered as Lalbag P.S. Case No. 940 dated 16.09.97. Subsequently by applying illegal force on the father of the plaintiffs the defendants got some paper signed by him to the effect that he would not proceed with the criminal case as well as civil suit. The defendants by putting threat on the life of the plaintiffs as well as their father Abdul Majid and also by applying force got a white paper signed by them with the writing to the effect “১৬,৬০,০০০/- টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম” though they received no money from the defendants. The defendants demolished the entire one storied building and the shop rooms standing on the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. Because of the eviction of the plaintiffs from their one storied building, from the semi pucca family quarters and the 13 (thirteen) shops on 16.09.97 the plaintiffs are being deprived of their monthly income to the tune of taka 26,000/-, so they were entitled to get mesne profit at the said rate from the said date.

6. By further amendment the plaintiffs added a prayer being prayer ka (1) (ka) to the effect:

"For declaration that the kabala executed through court on 27.02.1980 in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka and registered in the office of the District Registrar being deed No. 8119 of 1980 was fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon the plaintiffs."

7. The suit was contested by the defendants by filing a joint written statement denying the material statements made in the plaint and contending, inter-alia, that the plaintiffs had no cause of action to file the suit. The suit was not maintainable in its present form and was barred under the provisions of section 42 of the Specific Relief Act as well as section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The suit was also barred by limitation. The suit property along with other property which is known as No.1 Atash Khana Lane belonged to Binodini Daishaya, Shaym Chandra Shaha, Benu Lai Shaha, Brindaban Chandra Shaha, Shanatan Shaha, Kunaj Behari Shaha and Khiroda Shundari Daishaya. Khiroda Shundari Daishaya purchased the right, title and interest of Binodini Daishaya by a registered kabala being No. 2892 of 1899. Khiroda Sundari Daishaya also purchased the right, title and interest of Shayam Chandra Shaha by a registered kabala being No. 3070 of 1899. Benu Lal Shaha transferred his entire right, title and interest from C.S. plot No. 237 of C.S. khatian No. 40 to Rai Mohan Shaha. Subsequently Khiroda Sundari Daishaya by a registered kabala dated 22.09.1927 purchased the entire share of Benu Lal Shaha from Rai Mohan Shaha vide kabala No. 3430. Birendra died leaving behind his only brother Guru Charan Shaha to inherit his property. Guru Charan Shaha died leaving behind his wife Laxmi Daishaya who sold 3 (three) annas and 4 (four) gandas from the said plot to Sanatan Shaha. Sanatan Shaha became the owner of 6 (six) annas and 8 (eight) gandas share, 3 (three) annas 4 (four) gandas being through inheritance and the rest by purchase. Shanatan Shaha sold his said entire share from the said C.S. plot to Radha Ballav Shaha. Khiroda Sundari Daishaya purchased the rest portion of C.S. plot No. 40 of C.S. Khatian No. 237 from Radha Ballav Shaha by a registered kabala dated 04.03.1932 being kabala No. 738 and thus she remained in possession thereof as the rightful owner. Thereafter Kunja Behari Shaha died leaving behind his only son Lalit Mohan Shaha and widow Khiroda Sundari Daishya. Thus Khiroda Sundari Daishya became the 16 (sixteen) annas owner and remained in peaceful possession thereof. Khiroda sold the entire suit property to Salimunnesa on receipt of proper consideration by a registered kabala being No. 2042 dated 27.03.53 and delivered possession thereof to her. Salimunnesa while had been in possession of the suit property by paying rents transferred her 8 annas share to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8 (eight) annas to Mohammad Ilias on 15.06.1959. Mohammad Ilias by a registered deed of gift transferred his 8 (eight) annas share to Rasheda Begum and delivered possession of the same to her. Thus Rasheda Begum became the 16 (sixteen) annas owner of the suit property. Rasheda Begum remained in possession of the suit property by mutating her name and paying rents to the knowledge of all sun and dry. One Munjurul Hoq was the tenant in a portion of the suit property and as he defaulted in paying rent Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the Court of the then Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka for the realization of the arrear rent. In the same court Rasheda Begum also filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for eviction of her tenant. Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed created two forged registered agreements on 16.11.59 being No. 6904 and 6905 by forging the signature of Rasheda Begum. On the said date said Doctor Manjurul Haque also procured (in Bengali it has been written (সংগ্রহ করেন) two applications for compromise in the name of Rasheda Begum and Khatimunnesa respectively through forgery and under duress for filing the same in the money suit and the said house rent case. In the said compromise applications Doctor Manjurul Haque claimed that he purchased 7 (seven) annas share of the suit plot in the auction held on 18.06.53 and put heavy pressure upon Rasheda Begum to admit the fact of auction purchase. Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Dhaka praying for cancellation of the deeds of agreement dated 16.11.1959 and also the applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959. In the plaint of the said suit Rasheda Begum disclosed that the owners of No. 1. Atash Khaha Lane were Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash who sold the same to Salimunnesa on 27.05.1954. Defendant No. 2, Khatimunnesa of the said suit was the wife of Doctor Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed and was a tenant under Khiroda Sundari Daisyha and Lalit Mohan Dash and after the transfer of the suit property she became a tenant under Salimunnesa. Thereafter Salimunnesa sold her eight annas sha7re to Rasheda Begum and the rest 8 (eight) annas share to Md. Bias along with the right of tenancy of Khatimunnesa. Md. Ilias transferred his purchased share in favour of Rasheda Begum by way of gift and delivered possession thereof to her and thus Rasheda Begum became the 16 (sixteen) annas owner of the suit holding. As Khatimunnesa did not pay the house rent, Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the Court of Munsif 3rd Court, Dhaka for realization of the arrear rent and Md: Ilias filed House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 for eviction of Khatimunnesa. Monjurul Hoque was a wicked and greedy person and who in order to grabe the property of Rasheda Begum filed false and harassing complaint before the Anti-Corruption Department and the Martial Law News Centre. Rasheda Begum was a pardanishin lady. At the ill advice of Manjurul Haque the then-in-charge of Martial Law News Centre Major Sharif obtained the signatures of Rasheda Begum in two contract papers and compromise applications against her will by putting threat to her. The contents of the contracts and the compromise applications were not read over to Rasheda Begum. As the alleged contracts and the applications for compromise were created against the will of Rasheda Begum and by putting threat to her she filed Title Suit No. 221 of 1964. In the said suit Khatimunnesa and Doctor Manjurul Haque appeared and filed written statement claiming that they purchased 7 (seven) annas share of the suit holding in auction on 20.06.53. In the alleged auction sale Khiroda Sundari Daishaya and Lalit Mohan Daishaya were shown as judgment debtors though long before of 20.06.53 the suit holding was sold to Salimunnesa within the knowledge of Manjurul Haque and Khatimunnesa, so Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Dash had no ownership in the suit property consequently the purchase of 7 (seven) annas share from the suit holding was not correct. Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 was decreed on 25.12.65 in favour of Rasheda Begum declaring the registered agreements being Nos. 6904 and 6905 dated on 16.11.59 as cancelled and ineffective. In the said suit the trial court also declared the two compromise applications filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 59 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 as cancelled. Against the said judgment and decree Doctor Manjurul Haque and his wife Khatimunnesa filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge who heard the said appeal by his judgment and decree dated 19.07.66 dismissed the appeal affirming those of the trial court. Doctor Manjurul Haque and his wife filed Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 before the then High Court but the appeal was dismissed. Thus, the right, title and possession of Rasheda Begum in the suit property was confirmed. While Rasheda Begum had been in peaceful possession of the suit property to the knowledge of all sun and dry she entered into a contract with the defendants to sell the same at a price of taka 45,000/00 being the highest market value and on receipt of a sum of taka 15,000/00 as advance executed a bainapatra on 12.08.72. As Rasheda Begum killed time to execute and register the kabala on this or that plea the defendants filed Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for specific performance of contract. The said suit was decreed on 15.11.79. Subsequently the defendants got the kabala executed and registered on 27.02.1980 through court vide Title Execution Case No. 03 of 1980. After registration of the kabala through court when the defendants went to take possession of the suit property they having found some intruders in possession therein filed application before the executing court on 06.07.1980 to give them possession through court. Pursuant to the order of the executing Court when the bailiff of the court went to the suit property to give delivery of possession thereof the plaintiffs and the other goondas resisted the bailiff and threatened him with dire consequences. Under the above circumstances the bailiff returned the "writ of delivery" without executing the same with the prayer for police help. In the meantime the plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the court of Assistant Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for permanent injunction and obtained a decree which was set aside by the appellate court on 24.01.1987 in Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 filed by the defendants. The decree of the appellate court was upheld in Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 and in Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1992. After disposal of the said civil petition for leave to appeal the defendants filed application before the executing court on 07.03.93 for reviving the said execution case and pursuant to the order dated 16.10.93 a bailiff from the court went to the suit property on 21.10.93 to give delivery of possession thereof but the bailiff could not give delivery of possession due to the resistance put by Yousuf Kabir and 20/25 violators of law. The bailiff returned the writ of delivery of possession praying for police help. In the above circumstances the defendants prayed for police help to execute the decree and the Court allowed the prayer. The plaintiffs having lost up to the highest court of the country filed an application under Order XXI, rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure just to block the further proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. The application was rejected on 23.01.94 on contest. Thereafter the plaintiffs filed the instant suit making false and frivolous allegations just to hang on with their illegal possession in the suit property depriving the defendants to enjoy the fruits of the decree.

8. After amendment of the plaint the defendants filed additional written statement stating, inter-alia, that the plaintiffs used to live with their father in the same house. The plaintiff's father filed many other cases against the defendants making false statements which were dismissed upto the Appellant Division. The plaintiffs being in illegal possession of the suit property the defendants filed Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 to get possession of the same but they filed various suits against them just to harass them. The plaintiffs were not entitled to get any relief as prayed for including mesne profit. The defendants denied the claim of the plaintiffs that they were dispossessed by them by force from the suit property 16.09.97 and also the fact of looting away the goods from the suit property including from the tenanted rooms and shops causing financial loss to the tune of taka 20,00,000/00 (twenty lacs) and the fact of getting rents from the tenants to the tune of taka 26,000/00 per month. The defendants also denied the fact of existence of any one storied building, 10 (ten) pucca family quarter and 13 shop rooms on the suit land. When Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 was revived the plaintiffs filed an application for staying further proceedings of the same but their prayer was rejected on 29.01.1994. Against the said order the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 465 of 1994 before this Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.08.97 with direction upon them to hand over possession of the suit property to the defendants within 30 (thirty) days. As the plaintiffs did not agree to hand over possession of the suit property as per direction given by this Division Hajee Selim, a local member of the parliament mediated the matter and in presence of Alhaj Kazi Md. Masum, Commissioner of Ward No. 61, Md. Mosharaf Hossain ex-commissioner of Ward No. 61 and many other local respectable people, namely, Md. Uzir, Md. Yunuf, Md. Abdul Aziz, Md. Showkat and Md. Mesbah Uddin, the plaintiffs, their mother and their maternal uncle Abdul Ghani, the plaintiffs father Abdul Majid admitted that it was the defendants who were entitled to get the suit property. The plaintiffs father further told to give him some financial help on humanitarian ground so that he could settle some were else by purchasing land as well as to defray the educational expenses of the plaintiffs and their sister as they had no other house to live in, and if such help was given he would leave the suit property. On such proposal when Hajee Md. Selim wanted to know from the plaintiff s father the amount of compensatory costs he had to be given, he (Abdul Majid) after deliberation in a separate room with the plaintiffs, their mother and his brother-in-law demanded taka 20,00,000/00 (twenty lacs) only. Then Hajee Selim after discussing the matter with the said two Ward Commissioners and the local "Murabbis" told the defendants to pay the plaintiffs taka 15,00,000/00 (fifteen lacs). The plaintiffs having demanded taka 2,00,000/00.(two lacs) more Hajee Selim directed the defendants to 'Pay them taka 1,50,000/00 more and taka 10,000/00 as the costs for transporting the goods, that is, in total taka 16,60,000/00. In the shalish (as used in the additional written statement) it was further decided that the plaintiffs father would withdraw the civil and criminal cases at his own costs. After the defendants paid the plaintiffs father taka 16,60,000/00 on 30.09.97 at the direction of Mr. Hajee Selim and other "Murabbis he (Hajee Selim) got a paper written by the father of the plaintiffs acknowledging the receipt of taka 16,60,000/-which was also signed by the maternal uncle of the plaintiffs Abdul Gani. Subsequently on 05.10.97 plaintiff No. 2 himself put his signature in the said paper acknowledging the receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,000/-. Thereafter, from 01.10.97 to 04.10.97 the plaintiffs took away their furnitures and the other goods from the suit property to the house of their maternal uncle at Purana Paltan and handed over the vacant physical possession thereof to the defendants on 05.10.1997. Plaintiffs father had filed a false case against defendant No. 1 and others with Lalbag Police Station being Case No. 32(9)/97 which he withdrew on 12.10.97 as per the verdict of the salish. Pursuant to the decision of the Shalishdars as well as the direction and knowledge of the plaintiffs their father filed an application in the suit on 07.10.97 stating that he would not proceed with the suit and subsequently he also deposed in the suit to the said effect. Accordingly, the court below dismissed the suit. But long thereafter showing the plaintiffs major and on making false statements the suit was revived. As per the prayer of the defendants made in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 the bailiff delivered possession of the suit property to the defendants and accordingly, the said execution case was disposed of. After getting possession of the suit land and the other adjacent lands the defendants demolished the kucha and semi pucca rooms standing thereon and by investing some lacs of taka completed major works for constructing multistoried building and the remaining work was also under process.

9. At the trial the plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and the contesting defendants examined 9 witnesses. Both the parties filed documents which were marked as exhibits. The learned Subordinate Judge by the judgment and decree dated 31.03.2004 decreed the suit declaring plaintiff's 16 annas title to the suit property and also declaring the judgment and decree dated 15.11.79 passed by the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 without any basis, and ineffective. The court below further declared that by the decree passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 the plaintiffs and “নালিশী সম্পত্তি” were not bound (the ordering portion of the judgment has been written in the above term). The Court below further declared the proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 of the Court of the Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka without any basis and by the said execution proceeding the plaintiffs as well as “নালিশী সম্পত্তি” were not bound (the ordering portion of the judgment has been written in the above term). The Court below directed the defendants to hand over the possession of the suit property to the plaintiffs within 60 (sixty) days from the date of the judgment. The Court below also allowed the prayer for realization of mesne profit from the defendants for dispossessing the plaintiffs tenants on 16.09.97 from 10 family rooms and 13 shop rooms.

10. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and decree the defendants have preferred the instant appeal.

<u>11. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submitted that the plaintiffs claimed their title to the suit property on the basis of alleged auction sale which took place on 20.06.53, whereas the defendants vendor's vendor purchased the suit property from the admitted owners on 27.03.1953, therefore, the plaintiffs predecessor did not acquire any title to the suit property by virtue of the alleged auction purchase. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that previously the plaintiffs vendor's predecessor Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed made an attempt to nullify the result of Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 filed by the defendant's vendor Rasheda Begum against him and his wife by obtaining signatures on two applications showing withdrawal of the suit and the case which were ultimately set aside in Title Suit No. 221 of 1984 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka and thus the title of defendant's vendor was recognised in the said suit, the plaintiffs could not have any title through said Manjurul Haque, so their suit was liable to be dismissed. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that previously plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the present defendants which they lost up to the Appellate Division and moreso, in the alleged two agreements created by Ali Ahmed in the name of Rasheda Begum on 16.11.59 which were cancelled in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964, the plaintiffs predecessor Ali Ahmed having claimed 7 annas share only in the suit property by virtue of his alleged auction purchase the plaintiffs could not claim the entire suit property and in fact their suit was clearly barred by the principle of constructive resjudicata, and, as such, their suit was liable to be dismissed. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that the sale certificate allegedly issued in favour of Ali Ahmed does not tally with form 28 and rule 74 printed and framed respectively under the rules framed under the Public Demands Recovery Act, so the auction was doubtful and by such auction purchase no title accrued to said Ali Ahmed and consequently the plain-tiffs did not acquire any title to the suit property, therefore, they were not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that the plaintiffs having voluntarily vacated the suit property by delivering the possession thereof to the defendants on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,600/00 the instant suit for recovery of khash possession was not maintainable in law, the learned sub-ordinate judge erred in law in decreeing the suit and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside and the appeal be allowed.</u>

12. Mr. M.I. Faruqui, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondents, on the other hand, submitted that in deciding the merit of the appeal pleading of the parties has to be kept in mind. In paragraph 12 (ka) of the plaint which was added by way of amendment it was categorically stated that during the pendency of the suit the defendants along with their 20/25 accomplices being armed with dangerous weapons dispossessed the plaintiffs and their bharatias forcibly on 16.09.97 from the suit property and looted away the goods and then demolished the one storied building, the ten semi pucca family quarters and 13 shop rooms and that subsequently the defendants on the threat of life of the plaintiffs and their father got a writing in a white paper from them by force to the effect that they received a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 though actually they did not receive any such money, but the defendants in their additional written statement did not specifically deny the said statements as required by rules 3 and 4 of Order VIII of the Code of the Civil Procedure (the Code) and thus in fact they admitted the said assertions of the plaintiffs, the Court below rightly decreed the suit. Mr. M. I. Faruqui further submitted that plaintiffs' previous suit being Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 was for permanent injunction and though the same was dismissed upto the Appellate Division, yet in view of the observations made by it to the effect that a simple suit for permanent injunction notwithstanding the plaintiffs possession was not maintainable in the circumstances of the case the instant suit for declaration title and for recovery of khan possession along with the other reliefs was quite maintainable in law and, as such, the principle of constructive resjudicata has got no manner of application as sough to be argued by Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali. Mr. Faruqui further submitted that previously Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 106 of 1970 against Khatibunnesa and others for declaration of title which was dismissed for default, but no step was taken for revival of the suit, therefore, the defendants could not plead for title to the suit property in view of the provisions of section 12 read with rules 8 and 9 of Order 9 and rule 1 (3) of Order 23 of the Code. Mr. Faruqui by referring to the deposition of the plaintiffs witnesses submitted that they conclusively proved that the defendants took possession of the suit property by force, looted away the articles therefrom and thus they took law in their hand after having failed to get possession through court, therefore, the court below rightly decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiffs. Mr. Faruqui lastly submitted that the plaintiffs in support of their case of auction purchase by Ali Ahmed as far back as on 20.06.1953 filed all the relevant documents which included the sale certificate, the writ of delivery of possession and proved their continuous possession in the suit property since 1953 till they were dispossessed by the defendants forcibly and thus proved their title to the suit property, the court below rightly decreed the suit, so no interference is called for by this court with the impugned judgment and decree and the appeal be dismissed.

13. In view of the submissions of the learned Advocates of the respective parties we want to examine first whether the suit was barred under the principle of constructive res-judicata as argued by Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali. In order to decide the said point we must consider the nature of the suits fought between the parties prior to the instant suit, the issues framed therein and the findings given by the Court concerned. The first suit was Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 filed by Rasheda Begum against Monjurul Haque and his wife Khatibunnesa (in some places her name has been mentioned as Khatimunnesa) in the Court of Munsif, Dhaka. That suit was filed for declaration that the two deeds of agreement dated 16.11.59 executed by the plaintiff and defendant No. 1 'be void' and also for declaration that the petitions for compromise signed by the plaintiff and filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1951 of the Court of Munsif, Dhaka and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 before the House Rent Controller, Dhaka 'be void and not binding against the plaintiff' and also for cancellation of the said documents. The said suit was decreed on 25.12.65 on contest in the following terms:

"…………..That suit be decreed on contest against the defdts with costs. It is hereby declared that the two deeds of agreement executed between Rasheda Begum and Dr. Manjurul Haque, plff and defdt No. 1, on 16.11.59 and registered in Dacca Sadar Joint S.R. office in book No. 1 Volume No. 80 being deed No. 6904/59 and 6905/59 be void and inoperative and the same be delivered up and cancelled. It is further declared that the compromise petitions filed in H.R. Case No. 598/59 before the H.R. Controller and in M.S. No. 50/59 of the Munsif, 3rd Court, Dacca be void. Let a copy of this decree be sent to the Sadar Joint Sub-Registrar, Dacca, for making a note and also to the court to Munsif, 3rd Court and to the H.R. Controller or making note.

14. The judgment passed in the suit has been [Barked as 'exhibit 'Uma'. From the judgment it appeared that in the said suit 4 issues were framed which are as under:

"1. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

2. Is the suit barred by limitation?

3. Are the impugned documents vitiated by fraud, coercion and undue influence and are they void, illegal and liable to be set aside?

4. Is the plff entitled to the decree as prayed for?"

15. Against the judgment and decree passed in the said title suit Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed and his wife filed Title Appeal No. 50 of 1966 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The appeal was dismissed by the learned subordinate judge 4th Court, Dhaka who heard the same. The judgment passed in the said appeal has been marked as exhibit 'Cha'. From the judgment it appeared that 3 (three) point were formulated for decision. The points were:

"1. The suit is bad for misjoinder of causes of action.

2. The suit is barred by limitation.

3. The impugned documents were not vitiated by fraud, coercion and undue influence and, as such, these ought not to have been cancelled."

16. In Second Appeal No. 1095 of 1966 filed before the then High Court of Judicature at Dhaka the judgment and decree passed in the said appeal was affirmed. The certified copy of the judgment has been marked as exhibit 'Cha (1). A reading of the judgments as referred to above does not show that any issue was framed as to the title of the parties to the suit property and as to the validity or propriety of the auction sale in which Ali Ahmed claimed to have purchased the suit property and in fact no conclusive decision was also given by any of the courts on the said two vital issues, as the reliefs sought for did not demand so.

17. The second suit fought between the parties was Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 filed by the plaintiffs in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The said suit was for permanent injunction so that the defendants could not dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property. The suit was decreed on 28.03.84. Against the said decree the defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge who heard the said appeal by his judgment and decree dated 24.01.87 allowed the appeal and dismissed the suit by setting aside the judgment and decree passed by the trial court. The concluding portion of the judgment is as under:

"From the facts circumstances evidence as well as materials on record I am led to believe that the suit for permanent injunction simpliciter is not at all maintainable. To my mind complicated question of law as well as facts involves in this suit. So the plaintiffs ought to have institute (sic) a suit for establishment of their title.

The Id. Munsif appear to have traveled (sic) beyond the scope of the suit and she was not justified in decreeing the suit. There is merit in the appeal which shall be allowed."

18. Against the said judgment and decree of the appellate court the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before this Division and a learned Single Judge who heard the said revision by his judgment and order dated 27.05.1992 discharged the rule and thus up-held the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court. The judgment passed by the appellate court has been marked as exhibit 'Nia. The learned Single Judge while affirming the judgment and decree passed by the appellate court clearly found to the effect:

“…………It is true that the plaintiffs are in possession but on the facts and circumstances and material evidence on record I am of the view that disputed question of title is very much involved in the present case which cannot be decided in a suit for permanent injunction. The plaintiffs ought to have instituted a regular suit to establish their title and possession instead of filing this suit for permanent injunction as a matter of testing device for ascertainment of title.  Since the lower Appellate Court after considering the material evidence on record found that present suit in the form of permanent injunction is not maintainable inasmuch as serious disputed question of title is involved, it is difficult for this revisional court to interfere with such finding of the lower Appellate Court. It is true that plaintiffs are in possession and filed suit for permanent injunction. Mr. Gafur submits that since the plaintiffs are in possession, they cannot be evicted by the defendants. It is now well settled that a person in possession of a property should be evicted in due process of law. So the plaintiffs are liable to be evicted in accordance with law.

………….. In view of the matter I do not find any substance in the present revisional application and I hold that the plaintiffs failed to make out a case for permanent injunction. The Court of Appeal below, in my view, has not committed any error of Law occasioning failure of justice in allowing the appeal and dismissing the suit of the suit of the plaintiffs."

19. Being aggrieved by the judgment and order passed in the said civil revision the plaintiffs preferred Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1992 before the Appellate Division. The Appellate Division while dismissing the leave petition observed as under:

“……….. The learned Subordinate Judge observed that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get a decree roe permanent injunction for their unspecified and unidentifiable 7 annas share (if at all) in view of these and other findings, we are of the view that it has been rightly decided that a simple suit for permanent injunction notwithstanding plaintiff s possession is not maintainable in the circumstances of the case."

20. A reading of the judgments passed in Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984, Civil Revision 76 of 1987 and Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1992 it is primafacie clear that the plaintiffs suit was dismissed as complicated questions of title were involved, but all the courts found their possession in the suit property. It is also a well settled legal proposition that in a suit for permanent injunction regarding an immovable property the court shall see whether the plaintiffs are in exclusive possession of the suit property and it can see title of the plaintiffs incidentally, so all the courts rightly refrained from giving any finding as to the title of the parties to the suit property as well as the auction purchase by Ali Ahmed on 20.06.1953. When all the 3 (three) courts dismissed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 on the categorical finding that complicated questions of title being involved the suit was not maintainable then how the stray observations even if any made regarding the auction purchase by plaintiffs vendor's predecessor Ali Ahmed can be said to be a constructive res-judicata to nonsuit the plaintiffs, the instant suit being one for title along with the consequential reliefs. We are of the view that in order to non suit the plaintiffs from maintaining a suit of the instant nature on the plea of constructive res-judicata as conceived of in explanation IV to section 11 of the Code the defendants were obliged to prove that in the earlier suit the plaintiffs did not at all plead their title on the basis of the auction purchase by their vendor's processor Ali Ahmed or that there was a conclusive decision in the previous suit on the title of the plaintiffs or the auction purchase but the plaintiffs could prove none. At the risk of repetition we hold that since no issue as to the title of the parties to the suit property and the auction purchase by Ali Ahmed was raised and decided in neither of the suits fought by the parties and the plaintiffs vendors vendor having pleaded in the very first suit his own right title to the suit property it cannot be said that the plaintiffs claim was barred by the principle of constructive res-judicata. So, we find no substance in the submission Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, on the first point and hold that the instant was quite maintainable in law.

21. Now let us see whether the plaintiffs proved their title to the suit property. The whole basis of the plaintiffs title to the suit property was the auction purchase by Ali Ahmed on 20.06.1953. Further case of the plaintiffs was that the sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953, the sale certificate was issued on 19.11.1953 and Ali Ahmed got possession of the suit property through court 20.01.1954 and since then he had been in possession thereof. After the death of Ali Ahmed his wife Khatibunnesa inherited his entire property and on her death Abdul Mannan, her full brother inherited the same. In support of the said case of the plaintiffs they filed the sale certificate (exhibit 2) and the writ of delivery of possession (exhibit 2 (ka). In the written statement exhibit 2 and 2 (ka) were not challenged as spurious or forged. In the deposition of D.W. 1 only a general denial was given to the effect:

“………. ইহা সত্য নয় যে, আলী আহম্মদ নিলাম খরিদ করিয়া ভোগ দখলে ছিলেন। তিনি, ভাড়াটিয়া হিসাবে ভোগ দখলে ছিলেন।”

22. From exhibit 2 it is clear that the sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953. From exhibit 2 it is further clear that the entire suit land measuring .568 ajutangsha was sold in auction and not 7 (seven) annas share out of the suit plot. From exhibit 2 it further appears that the said 568 ajutangsha was the 7th annas share of the "হিস্যে" of the touzi being No. 61/1 of Dhaka Collectorate. `Touzi' refers to a page of the register of the tenant. When a property is sold in auction giving specific description thereof and mentioning the area how can it be said that 7 (seven) annas share out of the plot mentioned in the schedule of the sale certificate was sold. Mr. A. J. Mohammad vehemently argued that since in the compromise applications dated 16.11.59 filed in Title Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 and in the two registered agreements of the same date Ali Ahmed claimed to have purchased 7 (seven) annas share out of the suit land, in no case the plaintiffs could claim more than said 7 (seven) annas share of the suit property. But we do not find any substance in the said submission of Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali, our reason being that when the alleged agreements and the compromise applications were cancelled at the instance of the defendant's predecessor Rasheda Begum in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 how reliance could be put on the said agreements and the compromise applications. Further as those were not filed in the instant suit neither the trial court had any chance to see the recitals therein nor this court has any chance to go through the same to verify the submission of Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali. In the plaint the plaintiffs claimed the entire suit property which is clearly mentioned in the sale certificate as well as in the writ of delivery of possession, but the defendants never challenged the identify of the suit property or the area of the suit property.

23. The submission of Mr. A. J. Mohammad Ali that auction purchase by Ali Ahmed being after the transfer of the suit property to Salimunnesa by the admitted rightful owners, namely, Khiroda Sundari Shaha and Lalit Mohan Das Shaha no title accrued to him appeared to us absolutely fallacious. Because, though the auction sale took place on 20.06.53, yet the number of the certificate case shows that it was started in 1952 being No. 60 of 1952-53. It is also very pertinent to keep in mind that before auction sale notice under section 7 of the Public Demands Recovery Act, 1913 (the Act) must have been served after observing the other requirements as mandated in sections 4, 5 and 6 of the Act. The said provisions of the Act deal with filing of certificate for public demand payable to the Collector, requisition for certificate in other cases and the filing of certificate on requisition. Rules framed under section 38 of the Act have provided the details as to how the notice under section 7 of the Act shall be served. Section 8 of the Act has clearly stipulated that from and after the service of notice of any certificate under section 7 of the Act upon a certificate debtor any private transfer or delivery of any of his immovable property situated in the district in which the certificate is filed, or of any interest in any such property, shall be void against any claim enforceable in execution of the certificate and the amount due from time to time in respect of the certificate shall be a charge upon the immovable property of the certificate-debtor, wherever situated, to which every other charge created subsequently to the service of the said notice shall be postponed. Section 9 of the Act has clearly provided for filing petition denying the liability and section 10 thereof has spelt out about the hearing and determination of such petition. The defendants in their written statement did not specifically challenge the auction sale, what they pleaded was that Ali Ahmed having earlier claimed that he purchased 7 (seven) annas share of the suit plot the plaintiffs could not claim the entire suit property. Whether the certificate of demand and certificate of requisition were filed before the certificate officer prior to the alleged sale by Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Shaha to Salimunnessa are questions of fact and as the defendants did not challenge the certificate proceedings in which Ali Ahmed auction purchased the suit property the plaintiffs were not required to prove all those facts. In support of the plaintiffs claim of title through auction purchase by Ali Ahmed they having filed the sale certificate and the writ of delivery of possession their onus was discharged. Further, as per the own admission of the defendants that Ali Ahmed disclosed the fact of auction purchase as far back as in 1959 when he allegedly created two deeds of agreements and two applications for compromise filed in Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and in House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 which were ultimately cancelled in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964, but Rasheda Begum never took any attempt to set aside the said auction purchase by Ali Ahmed. In this regard we like to observe that in a revenue matter proceeding follows the land not the person, so even if Khiroda Sundari Daishaya and Lalit Mohan Shaha sold the suit property prior to the auction sale but that shall not automatically make the auction sale a nullity. It was obligatory upon Rasheda Begum to take step to set aside the sale. In this regard we like point out that rule 39 of the Rules as detailed in schedule 11 to the Act which have binding effect in view of the provision of section 38 of the Act (hereinafter refereed to as the Rules) has clearly provided that if any claim is preferred to or any objection is made to the attachment or sale of, any property in execution of a certificate, on the ground that such property is not liable to such attachment or sale, the certificate officer shall proceed to investigate the claim or objection. Rule 40 has provided that the claimant or the objector must adduce evidence to show that (in case of immovable property) at the date of service of the notice under section 7 of the Act he had some interest in, or was possessed of, the property attached. Rule 41 has given power to the certificate officer to release the property from attachment or sale. Rule 43 has provided that the party against whom an order is made may instant a suit in a civil court to establish the right which he claims to the property in dispute, but subject to the result of such suit (if any) the order shall be conclusive. But Salimunnessa or Rasheda Begum did not take shelter under the said provisions of law to set aside the sale. In the Act or in the rules nothing has been provided for as to when an auction sale shall take its effect, but we can easily take the aid of section 65 of the Code which reads as under:

"65. where immovable property is sold in execution of a decree and such sale has become absolute, the property shall be deemed to have vested in the purchaser from the time when the property is sold and not from the time when the sale becomes absolute."

24. It is true that the auction sale in question was not held in execution of a decree of a civil court, but we do not see any wrong in borrowing the concept from the Code it being a civil proceeding and appeared to us quite akin to an auction sale held under the Code in execution of a decree. Mr. Mohammad Ali like a drowning man who catches a straw tried to challenge the auction sale by submitting that the sale certificate does not tally with Form 28 and Rule 74 of the Rules, so on such defective sale certificate the plaintiffs could not claim their title to the suit property. On such submission of Mr. Mohammad Ali we have examined the sale certificate along with the said form and the rule but we have not found any major deviation or noncompliance with the said form and the rule to make the sale certificate void or voidable. We are of the view that the moment the auction sale was confirmed it took its effect from the date of its sale on 20.06.1953 and it was also acted upon with the delivery of possession of the auction sold property. After all these years the defendants cannot be allowed to challenge the same and that too by way of oral submission through their learned Advocate and thus to deny plaintiffs title to the suit property.

25. Admittedly the plaintiffs had been in possession of the suit property which was clearly found by all the courts in connection with the proceedings which arose out of Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The plaintiffs by amending the plaint prayed for recovery of khas possession of the suit property and also for mesne profit stating categorically that the defendants dispossessed them and their tenants therefrom forcibly on 16.09.1997. All along plaintiff's case was that their predecessor's predecessor Ali Ahmed got possession of the suit property through court on the basis of his auction purchase and in support of their said case they filed the writ of delivery of possession, exhibit 2 (ka). From exhibit 1 (ka) and 1 (kha) it appears that the S.A. and R.S. khatians were prepared in the name of Ali Ahmed. Exhibit 5 shows that plaintiffs names were mutated and a new khatian being No. 197 was opened in their names. Exhibit 6-6 (Na) series show that Ali Ahmed paid rents to the government and then the plaintiffs paid rents to the government after mutation of their names. Exhibit 7-7 (Nia) series show that the holding in respect of the suit property was recorded with the Dhaka City Corporation in the name of the plaintiffs and they paid City Corporation tax. Exhibits 8. 9 and 10 series show that it is the plaintiffs who paid the utility bills such as Dhaka Was a, gas and electricity in respect of the suit property. Exhibits 11 and 12 series show that the plaintiffs inducted tenants in the suit property who paid rents to them. And those documents primafacie proved that it was Ali Ahmed and the plaintiffs who exercised their right of ownership in the suit property and had been in possession thereof uninterruptedly since the delivery of possession on 20.01.54 by virtue of the auction purchase. On the other hand, the contesting defendants failed to file a single scrape of paper to show that their so-called vendor Rasheda Begum and before that Salimunnesa ever exercised their right of ownership and possession in the suit property or that Ali Ahmed or his wife had ever attorned Salimunnessa as land lord after purchase from Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Shaha or they ever paid any rent to Rasheda Begum attorning as their land lord. Not only that the defendants also failed to file/produce any original deed of their alleged vendor Rasheda Begum. It is a well settled legal proposition that though the khatians and rent receipts are not the documents of title, yet they can very much be used for collateral purpose to prove title. The very fact that S.A. and R.S. khatians were prepared in the name of Ali Ahmed and he paid rents to the government and after his death the plaintiffs paid rents and they also paid other utility bills proved their title to the suit property. It is also a salutory legal proposition that possession follows title, so even if it is presumed for argument's sake that the plaintiff's vendor's vendor Ali Ahmed purchased the 7th share of the suit plot as argued by Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, yet due to the long and continuous uninterrupted possession in the suit property since 20.01.1954, the plaintiffs acquired absolute title to the suit property.

26. From the judgment passed in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964 it is apparent that Rasheda Begum filed Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 in the Court of the then Munsif 3rd Court, Dhaka for realization of arrear rent and also House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 in the same court for eviction of her tenant and although Ali Ahmed allegedly took attempt to nullify the result of the said suit and the house rent case by filing two compromise petitions and eventually the said two compromise petitions were declared cancelled in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964, yet thereafter no step was taken by her either to realize arrear rents from Ali Ahmed and his wife Khatibunnesa or to evict them from the suit property. From exhibit 13 it appeared that Rasheda Begum filed Title Suit No. 106 of 1970 on 13.04.70 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against Khatibunnesa and others for declaration of title and injunction. Exhibit 13 further shows that the said suit was dismissed for default on 28.06.72. The said fact was asserted in the plaint as well as in the deposition of p. w. 1. Rasheda Begum did not take any step to set aside the said order of dismissal by filing an application under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code. Exhibit 14, the application filed by the plaintiffs for the certified copy of the plaint of said Title Suit No. 106 of 1970 also shows that the said order of dismissal was passed on 28.06.72; the certified copy of the plaint could not be supplied as the record was destroyed. Rule 9 of Order 9 of the Code has clearly spelt out that where a suit is dismissed wholly or partly under rule 8 of Order 9 of the Code the plaintiff shall be precluded from bringing a fresh suit on the same cause of action. Section 12 of the Code has clearly debarred a plaintiff from instituting a further suit in respect of any particular cause of action where he is precluded by rules from instituting a further suit. In this regard we may also refer to the provision of sub rule (3) of Rule 1 of Order XXIII of the Code which is as under:

"Where the plaintiff withdraws from a suit, or abandons part of a claim, without the permission referred to in sub-rule (2), he shall be liable for such costs as the Court may award and shall be precluded from instituting any fresh suit in respect of such subject-matter or such part of the claim."

27. Thus, it appeared to us that in fact, Rasheda Begum defendant's so-called vendor abandoned her claim to the suit property by not taking any step to set aside the order of dismissal of Title Suit No. 106 of 1970. It is true that it is not the defendants who have come for title, but when they set up a specific case of their title to the suit property through Rasheda Begum by obtaining an ex-parte decree for specific performance of contract and tried to justify their possession in the suit property we can very much see whether their vendor had any right and title to the suit property. From the above, it is clear that Rasheda Begum failed to establish her title to the suit property, so how the defendants could claim title to the suit property through Rasheda Begum in their defence to deny the plaintiffs title when they proved their story of acquisition of title and possession in the suit property by filing documents without any gape right from the auction purchase of the suit property by, Ali Ahmed. In this regard it is also very pertinent to state that the plaintiffs in theft plaint categorically stated that after a few days of the liberation of Bangladesh Resheda Begum left Bangladesh for Pakistan Via Nepal and did not enter into any contract with the defendants to sell the suit property, but they created a forged bainapatra. P.W.1 also deposed in court to the said effect. But the defendants failed to produce any evidence whatsoever to show that at the time of bainapatra which was allegedly executed on 12.08.72 or thereafter Rasheda Begum was in Bangladesh. Rather, the evidence of D.W.1 in his cross-examination to the effect:

“……. প্রদঃ ‘ছ’ এর ১ম পাতার পিছনে পৃষ্ঠার রাশেদা বেগম ২৫/০৩/৭৫ ইং তারিখে স্বাক্ষর করিয়াছে মর্মে লিপি আছে। তখন রাশেদা ঢাকার কোথায় ছিল মনে নাই। প্রদ ‘ছ’ এর ২য় পাতায় উল্টে পৃষ্ঠার রাশেদা বেগমের নাম লিপি আছে। উক্ত ৩/১১/৭৬ ইং তারিখে রাশেদা বেগম কোথায় ছিল আমার মনে নাই্ ইহা সত্য নয় যে, পূর্বোক্ত ২টি মানি রিসিট একই কালিতে একই বৈঠকে ও একই  হাতে লিখা হইয়াছে। রাশেদা বেগম বায়না পত্র সম্পাদনের পর ১২/৮/৭২ ইং তারিখে খুব সম্ভবতঃ ডি ও এইচ এস তে ছিল। ………….উক্ত মোকদ্দমাটি দায়েরের পর রাশেদা বেগম কোথায় থাকিত সুনির্দিষ্ট ভাবে বলিতে পারিব না। পরবর্তীতে যে ডিক্রীজারী মামলা মূলে দলিলটি পাইয়াছি উক্ত ডিক্রীজারী মামলাটি দায়েরের সময় রাশেদা বেগম কোথায় থাকিত বলিতে পারিব না। উক্ত জারী মামলার দলিলে খসড়া কপি জারী হইয়াছিল। কোন ঠিকানায় জারী জারী হইয়াছিল বলিতে পারিব না। আমাদের দায়েরকৃত দেঃ ৬২/৭৯ নং মোকদ্দমার রাশেদা বেগমের ঠিকানা এই মহুর্তে বলিতে পারিব না। ইহা সত্য নয় যে, দেঃ ৬২/৭৯ নং মোকদ্দমা ও ডিক্রীজারী ৩/৮০ নং মামলা রাশেদা বেগমের উপর যোগাযোগী ভাবে নোটিশ জারী দেখাই���াছি। ইহা সত্য নয় যে, তখন রাশেদা বেগম বাংলাদেশে ছিল না বা আমাদের বায়া দলিল ও কাগজপত্র সমূহ তঞ্চকী ও অকার্য্যকর বা আমি মিথ্যা সাক্ষ্য দিয়াছি।”

corroborates the plaintiff's case that at the relevant time of execution of the alleged bainapatra by Rasheda Begum and during the period of filing of Title Suit No. 62 of 1979, at the time of passing of the decree as well as up to the execution and registration of the kabala in favour of the defendants she was not in Bangladesh. Our view is further strengthen from the further fact that Title Suit No. 106 of 1970 brought by Rasheda Begum was dismissed for default on 28.06.72, had she remained present in Bangladesh after liberation then she would not have allowed the suit to be dismissed for default. Further though the defendants filed the bainapatra, yet none proved the same and none deposed as to the fact of passing of consideration to Rasheda Begum as part performance of the contract. Since the plaintiffs were not party in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 filed by the defendants and they were claiming title to the suit property on the basis of a decree passed therein the plaintiffs had every right to challenge the propriety of the decree passed in the suit, particularly when they prayed for a declaration to the effect that they were not bound by the judgment and decree passed therein. As the plaintiffs challenged the bainapatra allegedly entered into by Rasheda Begum and the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 as fraudulent the onus was upon the defendants to prove that the bainapatra was genuine and the decree in the said suit was obtained in a regular course on due service of summons of the suit upon Rasheda Begum in Bangladesh but they failed to discharge the said onus. It is also very significant to state that the defendants could not file any original title deed of their alleged vendor Rasheda Begum which also creates primafacie doubt about their case of bainapatra entered into by Rasheda Begum.

28. We conclude by holding that the plaintiffs proved their 16 (sixteen) annas title to the suit property.

29. Now let us see whether the defendants dispossessed the plaintiffs and their tenants from the suit property forcibly on 16.09.97 or the plaintiffs themselves vacated the same on 05.10.97 on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 from the defendants on 30.09.97. Admittedly the plaintiffs had been in possession of the suit property. In Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 a single Bench of this Division gave a clear observation to the effect:

"…………..It is true that plaintiffs are in possession and filed suit for permanent injunction. Mr. Gafur submits that since the plaintiffs are in possession, they cannot be evicted by the defendants. It is now well settled that a person in possession of a property should be evicted in due process of law. So, the plaintiffs are liable to be evicted in accordance with law. "

30. So, the plaintiffs could not be evicted from the suit property other that due process of law. The defendants levied Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for execution of the decree. (b) D.W.5 appeared to us to be a very partisan and interested witness, he being the manager of Dodge Industrial Company of which the defendants were the directors who used to supervise the affairs of the company directly. This P.W. also had sworn affidavit on behalf of the defendants as their tadbirkar in Transfer Miscellaneous Case No. 38 of 2002 of the Court of District Judge, Dhaka.

(c) D.W.6 deposed in supposition without asserting the fact of payment and the writing by Abdul Majid and the maternal uncle of the plaintiffs in a positive manner. (d) Although all the 3 (three) D.Ws. were allegedly present at the salish, yet none figured as a witness in the document allegedly written and signed by Abdul Majid and plaintiff No. 2. Had they remained present definitely they would have figured as witnesses.

(d) Neither Hajee Selim nor the Ward Commissioners who were allegedly present in the salish figured as a witness in the said alleged writing.

42. The evidence of the D.W.S does not inspire confidence in our mind to believe defendant's case that the plaintiffs voluntarily handed over possession of the suit property to them on 05.10.1997 on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 (sixteen lacs sixty thousand), on 30.09.97, as it sounded absurd to us that when the plaintiffs fought upto the Appellate Division to maintain their possession in the suit property by filing Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendants and then filed application in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 so that they could not be evicted through the execution of the said case and fought upto this Division they would leave the same on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 the suit being ready for peremptory hearing. Defendant's story of delivery of possession by the plaintiffs also appear to us against the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business in relation to the facts of the case as articulated in section 114 of the Evidence Act. If the plaintiffs handed over the vacant possession of the suit property to the defendants voluntarily then why there should be “ভাংচুর” as deposed by P.W.3 and evident from exhibits 16, 17 and 18 series. Had such a huge amount been paid as a. prize for the compromise then it would have been written in a form of document signed by both the parties and duly witnessed by the witnesses stating in detail the terms of compromise and the fact of voluntary delivery of possession. And what prevented the defendants to take step to file a compromise application in the suit to dispose of the same as per terms of the compromise. We have seen the alleged writing of Mr. Abdul Majid as to the receipt of taka 16,60,000/00 allegedly paid to him by the defendants as a settlement to leave the suit property as incorporated in the additional paper book. It is to be noted that original money receipt was not filed but from the evidence of D.W.1 it appeared that the same was written on the pad of Hajee Selim local member of the parliament. Though a photostat copy of the same was allegedly filed when D.W.1 was examined, we could not find out the same from the record. However, the said writing is as under:

বাংলাদেশ জাতীয় সংসদ সচিবালয়

"I Mr. Abdul Majid (Babul) S/0 Late Abdul Mannan, 1/B Atash Khana Lane, Lalbagh, Received Tk. 16,60,000/- sixteen Lakh & sixty thousand only from, Akram Hossain S/o Deen Mohammad.

Sd/= Eligible

30.09.97

Sd/= Eligible

30.09.97

ষোল লক্ষ ষাট হাজার টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম

Sd/= Eligible

05.10.97"

<u>43. The very writing as relied upon by the defendants as a proof of their payment of taka 16,60,000/00 to the plaintiffs appeared to us shocking and repulsive. It is unbelievable that when the bailiff from the Court failed to deliver possession of the suit property due to the resistance put by the plaintiffs they would hand over vacant possession of the same to the defendants on the basis of a mere money receipt written on a pad of a local member of the parliament; and that to in four lines having no reference to the suit property and the names of the parties. None of the persons who were allegedly present in the salish including the local member of the parliament Hajee Selim and the local Ward Commissioner was examined in court. What business the local member of the parliament had to meddle in the matter when both the suit and the execution case were pending in Court. Further, from the evidence of the D.W.S it is apparent that the alleged salish was held only on one date, that is, on 30.09.97, if that be so, how is that on the same sitting such a huge amount could be arranged and given by the defendants. How did they know that there would be a settlement on that very date and they would be required to pay the said amount. How is that in the alleged money receipt Abdul Majid put his signature on 30.09.97, whereas defendant No. 2 put his signature on 05.10.97. Moreno, if possession of the suit property was delivered voluntarily as claimed by the defendants then there must be a paper showing delivery of possession by the plaintiffs or their father executed in favour of the defendants. In this regard it is very pertinent to state that after the plaintiffs failed to resist the proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 by filing an application under Order XXI, rule 99 of the Code they filed an application in the suit on 28.11.94 for temporary injunction praying for restraining the defendants from evicting them from the suit property till disposal of the suit. On the said application a notice was issued upon the defendants asking them to show cause within 10 (ten) days as to why an order of temporary injunction as prayed for shall not be granted. As the said application for temporary injunction could not be heard and the defendants were taking desperate attempt to dispossess them the plain-tiffs on 14.09.97 filed an application under section 151 of the Code praying for an order of temporary injunction with a prayer for ad-interim injunction so that they could not be evicted through the proceedings of Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. Copy of the said application was duly served upon the learned Advocate of the defendants. The court below fixed the said application for hearing on the next date, that is, on 07.10.97. In the meantime the plaintiffs were evicted on 16.09.97 and the reason for such action by the defendants is obvious. P.W.1, categorically asserted the said facts in his deposition but he was not cross-examined on the said facts. The fact of forcible dispossession is also borne out from the photographs taken from the suit property after the eviction and exhibit 18 series which show that the structures on the suit property were damaged by resorting to vandalism. D.W.1 also admitted that he did not protest the news item published in the two dailies, namely, the Bhorer Kagaz and the Inquilab in that respect. From the evidence as discussed hereinbefore, it appeared to us that the defendants by taking law in their own hands dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit property forcibly just to frustrate the result of the suit which is very much deplorable and shocking and if such action of the defendants is countenanced to that would bring the whole legal system of dispensation of justice through court into jeopardy.</u>

44. The fact that there was a one storied building, 10 (ten) family rooms and 13 (thirteen) shops in the suit property and after taking possession of the suit land those were demolished are also admitted by the D.W.S apart from the evidence of the p. w. s particularly,P.W.3, an independent and disinterested witness as already discussed hereinbefore. Therefore, we find no reason to disbelieve plaintiffs case that because of their forcible dispossession from the suit property by the defendants on 16.09.97 and then demolition of the 10 (ten) family quarters and 13 (thirteen) shop rooms they were deprived of monthly rent from the tenants and so they were entitled to get the mesne profit as decreed by the court below.

45. In view of the discussions made above, we hold that the court below rightly decreed the suit in the terms as noted at the very beginning of this judgment and, therefore, we do not see any reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and decree.

46. In the result this appeal is dismissed. The impugned judgment and decree is confirmed.

47. There will be no order as to costs.

48. Send down the lower court's record immediately.
